mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.5 million units for three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1.5M for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its previous 12-month maximum by at least 3% for two consecutive months signals a robust supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher (t-test p < 0.05) during periods when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month max by 3% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for two consecutive months, accompanied by a concurrent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000, signals a tight labor market that pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the monetary aggregate (proxied by the sum of M1 and M2, but here using FEDFUNDS and RSAFS as available proxies) signaled by a combined monthly decline of over 2% in short-term interest rates and a drop in savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average by more than 5%, indicates liquidity tightening, which depresses risk asset valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -0.02 AND RSAFS < 12-mo SMA -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A YoY increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 8% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% for three consecutive months signals a precautionary savings cycle, reducing near-term consumption and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY > 8% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for four consecutive months, without a corresponding acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 250,000, signals a mismatch in labor market absorption, which raises wage inflation and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with weak payroll growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1.5% combined with a concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 2 million units signals an acceleration in manufacturing and construction activity, boosting corporate earnings and supporting higher equity valuations over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher (t-test p < 0.05) during triggered periods.
